description.narrative:
The Digital Peace <(>&<)> Climate Resilience Academy equips 200 marginalised youth in Mandera North with digital skills, peacebuilding tools, and climate resilience knowledge. Through a blended approach of online modules, community Peace <(>&<)> Climate Labs, youth-led micro-projects, and digital storytelling,participants become Peace <(>&<)> Climate Ambassadors, reducing climate-related conflict and strengthening community cohesion. The model is scalable and shares lessons across Africa and Europe.
Goal: Strengthen youth-led peacebuilding and climate resilience in Northern Kenya through a scalable digital and community engagement model.
Objectives:Train 200 marginalised youth in digital skills, climate adaptation, and peacebuilding; establish 10 community Peace <(>&<)> ClimateLabs; implement 20 youth-led micro-projects; create a digital knowledge-sharing platform for cross-continental learning.
Activities: Co-creation workshops, digital module development, youth training, lab formation, youth-led micro-projects, digital storytelling,policy dialogues, and participation in the Global Link <(>&<)> Learn event.
After the grant ends, the project will continue through the Youth Peace <(>&<)> Climate Ambassadors, who will maintain the labs and lead community initiatives. Digital modules and toolkits will remain accessible online for ongoing learning. Partnerships with the Mandera County government, local NGOs, and community stakeholders will support resource mobilization, mentorship, and scaling. The model is designed to be replicable and low-cost, ensuring sustainability and long-term youth-led impact.

participating-org.narrative:
Vision: A peaceful, resilient, and digitally empowered Africa where youth lead climate action and community transformation.
Mission: To empower marginalised youth in Kenya and beyond with skills, knowledge, and leadership opportunities in peacebuilding, climate resilience, and digital innovation, fostering sustainable development and social cohesion.
Objectives: Train marginalised youth in digital skills, peacebuilding, and climate resilience. Promote youth-led community action projects addressing local climate and conflict challenges. Establish sustainable learning and innovation hubs for ongoing capacity building. Facilitate cross-continental knowledge exchange and advocacy for youth inclusion in decision-making.
Values: Youth Empowerment: Prioritising participation and leadership of young people. Innovation: Using technology and creative approaches to solve local challenges. Inclusion: Ensuring gender equality and opportunities for marginalised groups. Sustainability: Building long-term impact through community ownership and scalablemodels. Collaboration: Partnering with communities, government, and international actors to achieve shared goals.
ERGO International Peace Initiative (EIPI) is a youth-led organisation governed by a Board of Directors composed primarily of young leaders under 35years of age, ensuring that decision-making reflects the perspectives and priorities of youth. The Board oversees strategic planning, financial management, and policy compliance, while an operational team of youth professionals manages day-to-day activities, program design, and implementation.
Our operating framework emphasizes participatory leadership, with youth actively involved in co-creating programs, leading community projects, and mentoring peers. Gender equality is a core principle: women and girls hold leadership positions across all levels, including the Board, management, and project implementation teams. EIPI promotes transparency and accountability through regular reporting, monitoring <(><<)>(><(>&<)><(><<)>)> evaluation, and stakeholder engagement, ensuring that youth voices drive the organisation’s mission to empower marginalised communities.
